title: A root over a residue prime avoids the localization polynomial
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $f,g\in k[t]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] with $f$ monic (leading coefficient $1$), and let $L$ be a field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Suppose that for a finite indexed family $(\alpha_i)_{i\in I}$ of elements of $L$ the coefficient image of $f$ in $L[t]$ equals $\prod_{i\in I}(t-\alpha_i)$; the empty family is allowed. Let $f_1\in k[t]$ be irreducible, meaning nonzero, not a unit, and with a unit factor in every factorization in $k[t]$. If $f_1\mid f$ and $f_1\nmid g$, then there is an index $i\in I$ such that $f_1(\alpha_i)=0$ and $g(\alpha_i)\ne0$, where evaluation uses the given map $k\to L$.
